extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners working on long-form story generation
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating models that recursively generate paragraph-by-paragraph long stories with explicit control over length while maintaining coherence and producing appropriate endings (completeness). Includes architectural components (CWC, LSP), datasets, and automatic evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural flow between paragraphs; whether consecutive paragraphs form a coherent progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring method: construct true pairs (two consecutive paragraphs) and fake pairs (two randomly selected paragraphs), train GPT-2 as a classifier to distinguish true vs fake pairs, and convert the classifier output to a score ∈ [0,1] with a sigmoid. Higher score = better coherence. Empirical notes: Memory (M) is central to capturing natural flow (ablations show LongStory¬M drops coherence); balancing long- and short-term contexts affects coherence. Report coherence per-length (e.g., 5,10,20,30,50 paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to conclude a story appropriately — producing a proper last paragraph/ending for stories of any length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paper introduces completeness as a new open-domain metric. Scoring method: same GPT-2 classifier approach as coherence, but true folds are last paragraphs and fake folds are non-last paragraphs. Reported completeness = (last paragraph's completeness score) − (average completeness score of non-last paragraphs). This formulation rewards producing distinctive, appropriately 'final' last paragraphs. Ablation notes: combination of Memory and Cheating plus LSP tokens improves completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitiveness (in-SELF BLEU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of internal repetition/diversity within a single generated document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute n-gram BLEU by taking one paragraph as hypothesis and the rest of the paragraphs in the document as references, then average across paragraphs — called in-SELF BLEU. Higher in-SELF BLEU implies more repetition (less diversity). Distinct from prior self-BLEU which treats whole documents differently. Empirical notes: Cheating (short-term context) helps reduce repetition; LongStory generally reduces repetitiveness compared to baselines for longer outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance (ROUGE scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: How well the generated document reproduces content relevant to the golden label / how well keywords map to generated text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L between generated documents and golden labels to assess relevance. Caveat: n-gram overlap metrics like ROUGE may penalize creative/novel but valid stories; therefore they should be complemented by coherence/completeness metrics. Use ROUGE results alongside other metrics when comparing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence, Completeness, and Repetitiveness as primary evaluation dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat coherence, completeness, and repetitiveness as the core automatic metrics for long story generation beyond conventional n-gram scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper argues these three capture properties n-gram metrics miss (completeness is newly emphasized). Report all three across target lengths to characterize model performance on long-form generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence scorer procedure (implementation detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational procedure to compute coherence scores using a learned classifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create dataset of paragraph-pairs: positive = consecutive paragraphs, negative = random pairs. Train a GPT-2 classifier on this task and convert classifier outputs via sigmoid into a [0,1] coherence score. Use consistent construction across datasets and lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness scorer procedure (implementation detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational procedure to compute completeness scores using a learned classifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create dataset of paragraph instances: positive = last paragraphs, negative = non-last paragraphs. Train GPT-2 classifier and convert outputs via sigmoid. Report completeness as last-paragraph score minus average non-last score to emphasize distinction between endings and body paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long and short-term contexts weight calibrator (CWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A module (implemented with BERT-tiny) that calibrates how much the model uses long-term Memory (M) vs short-term Cheating (C) vs input embeddings when generating each paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CWC input: discourse tokens (LSP) and the last generated paragraph; pooler output of BERT-tiny is used to determine β (learnable) and, with α hyperparameter, γ = 1 − α − β. Final attention combination: LM(X_t,M_t,C_t) = α Attention(Q,K,V) + β Attention(Q,M_t,M_t) + γ Attention(Q,C_t,C_t). CWC is trained jointly (BERT-tiny fine-tuned with same negative log-likelihood loss). Augmented CWC variants (making α learnable) can improve ROUGE but may hurt coherence and completeness — indicating trade-offs between relevance and narrative quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long story structural positions (LSP) / discourse tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit structural positional information per paragraph via discourse tokens to inform the generator about paragraph order and macro-structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tokens: <intro>, <body>, <tail>, and more fine-grained tokens <front>, <middle>, <ending>, <next-is-ending>. Mapping: <intro> = first paragraph; <tail> = last paragraph; <front>/<middle>/<ending> split the document roughly into thirds (first 1/3, next 1/3, last 1/3); <next-is-ending> labels the paragraph immediately before the end. More granular tokens were added because a single <body> token is insufficient for representing many-paragraph documents. Ablations show LSP tokens help completeness and reduce repetition, though in some cases they may slightly reduce ROUGE (relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory (M_t) — long-term context vector
rubrics_metrics.description: A memory vector that stores long-term context across paragraphs to sustain a broad understanding of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mt is initialized and updated using gated updates (gt, ˆM_t formulas; see paper) akin to Plotmachine. It is incorporated into attention via weighted attention (β). Empirical note: Memory contributes strongly to coherence (LongStory¬M performs worse on coherence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cheating (C_t) — short-term context window
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term context constructed from embeddings of the most recent generated tokens/paragraphs to preserve local continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ct = tanh(Emb(last c paragraph tokens...)). c is a hyperparameter (here up to last three paragraphs). Incorporated into attention via weight γ. Empirical note: Cheating helps local continuity, improves relevance in some ablations, and reduces repetition by preventing over-attending to older contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursive paragraph generation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The model must generate each paragraph recursively: produce paragraph t using previous paragraphs' contexts plus inputs (keywords + discourse tokens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulation: input X_t = (keywords with [SEP] tokens, discourse token(s)), generate Y_t conditioned on previous paragraphs and X_t. Recursive generation introduces information-leak/forgetting challenges that architectures must mitigate (hence Memory and Cheating). Evaluate across multiple target lengths to ensure robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of keywords (whole-story keyword input) for planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use extracted keywords representing the entire story as input to guide paragraph generation without providing a full plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords are extracted (RAKE used in experiments) and concatenated with discourse tokens to form X_t. The model must produce paragraphs consistent with the keywords; ROUGE vs golden labels is used to measure how well keywords drive generation (relevance). This enables more challenging open-domain generation vs methods that require detailed outlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and dataset diversity recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Train on datasets with varied average document lengths to learn representations across length scales and support zero-shot generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper trains on Writing Prompts, Booksum (chapters), and Reedsy Prompts, using consistent segmentation into paragraphs (max 200 tokens each). Combining datasets (Total) improved zero-shot performance on other dataset types versus single-dataset trained models. Recommendation: include diverse length distributions during training to improve generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation hyperparameters and decoding settings to reproduce results
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific training and decoding practices found useful for the task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training: teacher-forcing used so labels are used for contexts during training. Hyperparameters: α set to 1/2 in main experiments; cheating window c up to last three paragraphs. Decoding: beam sampling with top_k=50, top_p=0.95, no_repeat_ngram_size=3, repetition_penalty=3.5. These settings contributed to reported performance and are recommended when reproducing experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation and evaluation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically ablate model components to quantify their contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create variants: LongStory¬M (no memory), LongStory¬C (no cheating), LongStory¬D (no new discourse tokens). Compare across ROUGE, in-SELF BLEU, Coherence, Completeness, and Avg paragraph length across multiple target paragraph lengths. Use ablations to draw conclusions about which components most affect coherence, completeness, relevance, and repetitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of n-gram metrics for long-form story evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Caveat that traditional n-gram matching metrics (ROUGE, BLEU) do not fully capture story quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note that well-crafted stories may diverge from golden labels and thus score poorly on ROUGE/BLEU despite being good. Therefore, complement ROUGE with coherence/completeness/repetitiveness metrics. Use human evaluation or learned discriminators where possible to capture narrative quality beyond n-grams.
